If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted decline in late horizon (week 3–4) by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted rise in mid horizon (week 2) by 5–10% to compensate for bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 2 days, shift forecast peak earlier by 1–2 days and reduce peak magnitude by 5–8%.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) across 5+ days, apply linear smoothing to forecast path to reduce volatility in late horizon.  
If forecast consistently underestimates true values in early horizon (first 5 days), add 2–3% to each early forecast to align with sentiment-driven momentum.  
If forecast consistently overestimates true values in late horizon (last 5 days), subtract 3–5% from each late forecast to reflect sentiment-induced correction.
